category_title: Middle school students who disengage and use ritualistic rule-following when encountering fractions
scenario_title: Explaining fraction comparisons with visual drawings
minimal_context: Idit is in a one-on-one interview using circle drawings to explain whether 2/9 or 3/4 is bigger.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at these fractions. Can you draw circles to show 2/9 and 3/4 and tell me which one is bigger?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: And then if I have, uh... (draws circle with four small circles in it) four... and I draw um three (colors three of the four circles)...

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: So um... (raises eyebrows while looking at her drawing, tilts her head) my opinion is that this is bigger (points to the 2/9 drawing).

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why? How is it derived from this drawing?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues looking at the drawing, tilts her head), um-hm... (chuckles, then sits up, mumbling) I don't know, that's how I thought of it... (Smiling, mumbles) I don't know, there are things I can't do.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's look at these fractions. Can you draw circles to show 2/9 and 3/4 and tell me which one is bigger?

STUDENT: And then if I have, uh... (draws circle with four small circles in it) four... and I draw um three (colors three of the four circles)...

TUTOR: Okay, what do you think?

STUDENT: So um... (raises eyebrows while looking at her drawing, tilts her head) my opinion is that this is bigger (points to the 2/9 drawing).

TUTOR: Why? How is it derived from this drawing?

STUDENT: (Continues looking at the drawing, tilts her head), um-hm... (chuckles, then sits up, mumbling) I don't know, that's how I thought of it... (Smiling, mumbles) I don't know, there are things I can't do.

task.content: Explaining why 2/9 is bigger than 3/4 using circle drawings

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When asked to explain reasoning ('Why? ...how is it derived from this drawing?')
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: (Continues looking at the drawing, tilts her head ), um-hm ...(chuckles, then sits up, mumbling) (I) don't know, that's how I thought of it.

behavior_patterns.condition: When reaching a dead end in explanation
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: (Smiling, mumbles ) (I) don't know, there are things I can't do.
